title: Interactive and file-based Gen AI decoys: types, datasets, limits, deployment targets and testing

prose.text: {{types}} {{personality}} The MCP server decoy is in [[deception.mcp-server-decoys]].

prose.label: Related.
prose.text: The decoy types that host them are in [[deception.network-decoys]] and [[deception.ti-decoys]]; starting and stopping is in [[deception.decoy-deployment]]; the hub is [[deception.overview]].

types.statement: Deception supports interactive Gen AI decoys (chatbots, LLM servers, open-source platforms; deployable on Internal, Zero Trust Network (ZPA) or TI decoys) and file-based Gen AI decoys (resources used to set up local LLMs).

quotes: Interactive Gen AI Decoys: Mimics common interactive Gen AI infrastructure such as chatbots, LLM servers, open-source platforms, etc.
Internal Networks via Internal Decoy
Zero Trust Exchange via Zero Trust Network (ZPA) Decoys
Internet via Threat Intelligence (TI) Decoys
File-Based Gen AI Decoys: Mimics resources that are used to set up local LLMs.

file-assets.statement: File-based Gen AI decoys are created from Gen AI file datasets on endpoints via landmine policies, Azure storage account container or file share decoys, AWS S3 decoys, or network decoys via FTP or Share service.

quotes: Endpoints via landmine policies
Azure Cloud via storage account container decoy or storage account file share decoy
Amazon Web Services (AWS) Cloud via S3 decoys
Network decoys via FTP or Share service

personality.statement: Deception provides a Gen AI network decoy personality usable in manual network decoy configuration or in a deception strategy.

quotes: Deception provides a Gen AI decoy personality that serves as templates to deploy Gen AI decoys via network decoys.
You can use this personality when configuring network decoys manually, or use them in a deception strategy to create decoys.

threatparse-rule.statement: Deception captures the prompt sent to a Gen AI decoy and categorizes it with the Gen AI Malicious Input Prompt ThreatParse rule; the malicious classification and category come from enrichment with Deception AI, so the gen ai malicious and gen ai malicious category values might be inaccurate.

quotes: the classification of whether the prompt is malicious and the categorization of the prompt are determined by enriching data using Deception AI.
Hence, the values for the gen ai malicious and gen ai malicious category fields might be inaccurate.
It also captures the prompt and automatically categorizes it as malicious, etc. for further investigation using the Gen AI Malicious Input Prompt ThreatParse rule.

ai-disclaimer.statement: The vendor states content generated by the Deception AI is informational only and prone to inaccuracy and AI hallucinations.

quotes: The content is prone to inaccuracy and AI hallucinations.
The responses or content generated by the Deception AI is for informational purposes only.

datasets.statement: The interactive Gen AI application datasets are ChatBot (high-interaction) and Apache Airflow, Bento Frontend, ClearML, GitLab GenAI, JupyterHub, Metaflow, MLflow and Ray Serve (static).

quotes: | ChatBot | High-interaction |
| Apache Airflow | Static |
| Bento Frontend | Static |
| ClearML | Static |
| GitLab GenAI | Static |
| JupyterHub | Static |
| Metaflow | Static |
| MLflow | Static |
| Ray Serve | Static |

high-interaction-limit.statement: Up to three interactive Gen AI decoys using the high-interaction dataset can be deployed with Private Access and Internal decoys combined; the count for static datasets depends on the licensing agreement.

quotes: You can deploy up to three interactive Gen AI decoys using the high-interaction dataset with Private Access and Internal decoys combined.
the number of Gen AI decoys you can create using static datasets depends on your organization's licensing agreement.

no-tls.statement: Interactive Gen AI decoys using high-interaction datasets do not support TLS, so TLS ports such as 443 should not be used.

quotes: Interactive Gen AI decoys that are deployed using high-interaction datasets don't support the TLS protocol. When configuring these decoys, don't use TLS ports (e.g., 443).

ti-static-only.statement: Internet-facing Gen AI decoys via TI decoys use a Gen AI static application dataset; out-of-the-box high-interaction datasets are not supported for TI decoys.

quotes: Out-of-the-box Gen AI high-interaction datasets are not supported for TI decoys.
select a Gen AI static application dataset from the drop-down menu.

file-datasets.statement: The Gen AI file datasets added are Falcon-7b (an LLM from the Technology Innovation Institute) and GPT-2 Large (an LLM from OpenAI).

quotes: | Falcon-7b | An LLM developed by the Technology Innovation Institute (TII) for use in summarization, text generation, and chatbots. |
| GPT-2 Large | An LLM developed by OpenAI optimized for generating high-quality, context-aware text across diverse applications. |

endpoint-max-two.statement: At most two preconfigured file dataset decoys can be deployed on each endpoint, and if more than two are configured any two are selected at random.

quotes: You can deploy a maximum of two preconfigured file dataset decoys on each endpoint. If more than two preconfigured file dataset decoys are configured, any two files are selected at random.

cloud-prereq.statement: Deploying file-based Gen AI decoys to Azure or AWS requires cloud deception to be set up with that provider first.

quotes: Before deploying a file-based Gen AI decoy in the Azure cloud, ensure that you have set up cloud deception with Microsoft Azure.
Before deploying a file-based Gen AI decoy in the AWS cloud, ensure that you have set up cloud deception with AWS.

cloud-lure-pointing.statement: Azure file-based Gen AI decoys can be pointed to from landmine policies via cloud lures or session lures, and AWS ones via session lures.

quotes: File-Based Gen AI Decoys on Microsoft Azure
you can point to Gen AI decoys via landmine polices via cloud lures or session lures.
File-Based Gen AI Decoys on AWS
you can point to Gen AI decoys via landmine polices via session lures.

ztn-file-service-scope.statement: On the Gen AI file-decoy page the Zero Trust Network FTP and Share procedures begin "Create a Zero Trust Network decoy." and their lead-in reads "To deploy a file-based Gen AI decoy via an internal network decoy:".

quotes: To deploy a file-based Gen AI decoy via an internal network decoy:
Create a Zero Trust Network decoy.
evidence.after: File-Based Gen AI Decoys as an FTP Service on Zero Trust Network

quotes: To deploy a file-based Gen AI decoy via an internal network decoy:
Create a Zero Trust Network decoy.
evidence.after: File-Based Gen AI Decoys as a Share Service on Zero Trust Network

test-file-based.statement: To test a file-based Gen AI decoy deployed through a landmine policy, find an active agent with a matched policy under Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agents, note the file path shown in the Details pane, open the file in Windows PowerShell on the endpoint, and verify the event on the Deception dashboard.

quotes: In the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal, go to Settings > Endpoint Settings > Agents.
Locate an active agent with at least one matched policy in the Matched Policy column, and click the View icon under the Actions column.
On the Details pane that appears, ensure that the File Decoys module with Pre-Configured Datasets is configured in the landmine policy.
The landmine policy must have been deployed to the endpoint based on the selection criterion.
To test the decoy, make a note of the file path displayed in the Details pane.
Open Windows PowerShell on the endpoint in which you want to test the decoy.
The file is opened, and an event is generated in the Deception Admin Portal.
Verify the event on the Deception dashboard.
evidence.after: To test a file-based Gen AI decoy:

test-interactive.statement: To test an interactive Gen AI decoy, browse to the IP address or FQDN of the internal or Zero Trust network decoy with Gen AI service enabled, interact with it, and check the Investigate dashboard.

quotes: In the browser address bar, enter the IP address or FQDN for the internal or Zero Trust network decoy that has the Gen AI service enabled.
Go to the Investigate dashboard, locate the event corresponding to the interaction with the interactive Gen AI decoy, and verify the details.
